title: Lübeck, from the Lübeck/Hamburg plate in Civitates Orbis Terrarum vol. 1
notes: Braun & Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum vol. 1 (Köln, 1593), shelfmark A 330 A Folio RES::1-2, DOI 10.11588/diglit.12704, CC Public Domain Mark 1.0. Lübeck and Hamburg share ONE engraved sheet (page 24a), so this row and its twin cite the same object. The plate was viewed, not just catalogued. The Lübeck cartouche reads 'LVBECA VRBS IMPERIALIS LIBERA, CIVITATVM WANDALICARVM ET INCLYTAE HANSEATICAE SOCIETATIS CAPVT' - a contemporary witness naming the city head of the Hanseatic societas, which is an essay claim in its own right and should get an evidence row.

title: Hans Holbein the Younger, Der Kaufmann Georg Gisze
notes: Strongest London Kontor witness found: the museum record states Gisze went in 1522 to the Stalhof, the German merchants' establishment in London, and Holbein painted him there in 1532. NOT rights-cleared - the page licenses the image CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 while only the metadata is CC BY, and non-commercial fails the open-rights bar. Clearing this needs either a differently licensed reproduction or permission from the Gemäldegalerie. No IIIF manifest; the advertised endpoint returns 'This resource does not exist'.

title: Hanseatic privilege or charter
notes: Still unidentified. The one candidate surfaced this pass was Archiv der Hansestadt Lüneburg's transsumpt of King Sigismund's 1417 privilege (DDB NZVAG2O75AN5WTE6GB3KNTOICDX6AU3W), rejected on two counts: it is a Lüneburg salt-transport privilege rather than a Hanseatic trading grant, and it is licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.
